> Pick My Secret Santa is a free Secret Santa draw tool. Add names and a budget. The draw is picked in your browser, and the names and matches are stored on our server for the private links, in a form we can read.
> Each person gets a private link with their match, plus six gift ideas inside the budget. A private link is hidden from plain sight, not locked; anyone with a link can open it.
> Gift ideas come from a fixed list of 212 ideas. No ads, no accounts, no store links.
> Generated 2026-11-19 from the live pages at pickmysecretsanta.com.
> Contact: hello@pickmysecretsanta.com

## MCP server (for AI assistants)

Pick My Secret Santa also runs an MCP server: https://mcp.pickmysecretsanta.com/mcp. An assistant can call three tools there:

- pick_secret_santa_gift: gift picks from the same vetted bank of 212 ideas the site uses, by budget, who the gift is for, and what they are into.
- explain_secret_santa_rules: answers on the rules and on secrecy, by topic.
- plan_secret_santa_setup: checks a group (names, budget, pairs to keep apart) and returns a pre-filled draw link for the site.

The secret draw itself runs on the website, not in the MCP. The draw runs in the visitor's browser. On the website, short links store each name and match on our server, in a form we can read, so the links can open. The MCP itself never draws and never sees a match. The MCP helps with gift picks, rules, and setup. The drawing stays on the site.

What are they into?

Keep it secret.
If you lose this link, ask your organizer to send it again — they can.
Give it without giving yourself away
Pick the way that fits your place.
Desk drop. Leave it on their desk before work starts. Slip away before they sit down. Best when you know their start time.
Doorstep drop. Set the gift at their front door. Knock once, then walk away fast. Rain coming? Put it under cover first.
Front desk hold. Leave it with the front desk or mail room. Ask staff to hand it over later. Put only their name on the label.
Helper handoff. Ask a friend outside the game to deliver it. They say one line only: this is for you. Pick someone who will not spill the name.
Locker stash. Slip it into their locker, cubby, or drawer. Use a spot they open every day. Make sure no one else can reach it.
Mailbox surprise. Drop it in their work mailbox slot. Add a tag that says: open later, alone. Small, soft gifts fit this way best.
Plain mail box. Mail it in a plain, sturdy box. Write no return name or address. Post it early. Holiday mail runs slow.
Clue trail. Hide the gift somewhere safe nearby. Leave a first clue where they will see it. Each clue leads to the next one. The last clue leads to the gift.
Decoy box. Put the gift inside a bigger, silly box. Wrap that box in plain paper. The odd shape hides what is inside. Add soft filler so nothing rattles.
Gift table drop. Put it on the shared gift table early. Arrive before your person does. Then join the crowd like everyone else.
For every way: use plain wrap. Print the tag. Handwriting gives you away.
When you swap gifts
Pick one game for the whole group.
Guess first. Open one gift at a time, in turns. Each person guesses their Santa first. Only then does the Santa speak up.
Tag clue round. Write one clue on the gift tag. Read the tag aloud before opening. The group guesses from the clue alone.
Three clues game. Each Santa gives three clues, one by one. Clues start hard and get easier. The person guesses after each clue.
Note inside the wrap. Hide a signed note inside the wrapping paper. Your person finds it while they open. Keep the outside of the gift blank.
Stand and point. After the last gift, all Santas stand up. Each person points at their best guess. Santas sit down when guessed right.
Balloon pop. Put each Santa name inside a balloon. Each person pops one after opening their gift. The name inside names their Santa.
Video reveal. Film a short clip before the party. Start in a hat or a mask. Take it off and say your name. Play the clips after the last gift.
All at once. Tell everyone at once after the last gift. No guessing, no games, all names together. A Santa can stay secret if they want.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/privacy

Privacy - Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
EN|ES|PT
Privacy
The short version: The draw is made in your browser, and new draws also make short links. For a short link, our server stores your name and your match under a random code, in a form we can read; the address itself holds nothing readable, but we run this server, so we can read what is stored. Anyone with a link can open that link's match, and the organizer's group link can reach every person's link, so it can reach every match. Cloudflare Web Analytics counts visits here, and PostHog counts draws, shares, and link opens, as counts only. A draw notes which of its links were opened, by random code only. There are no accounts here.
What the draw does
You type in the names, a budget, and any pairs who should not draw each other, and the draw math runs in your browser. To make the short links, our server stores each name and match in a form we can read.
You can also say what a person is into, in your own words. In the draw tool, those words are matched on this device; they are not sent or saved, and no name is asked for there. If you use the Ask panel instead, your words go to this site's AI, which reads them and picks from the site's gift list, and nothing you type in the Ask panel is saved.
After a draw, your browser saves your links on this device only, so you can send a link again later. You can clear them any time with two taps. On a shared device, clear them when you are done.
Private links
Each link shows one person's match, and no one else's. With a long link, the match sits inside the link itself, in coded words after the # mark. That part is not sent to our server when the link opens, but anyone who holds the link can read it.
New draws also make a short link for each person. A short link's address holds only a random code, and nothing in it can be read. Your name and the name you drew sit on our server under that code, in a form we can read; we run this server, so we can read the names and matches stored for short links. That record also holds the group's names, so whoever opens the link can start their own draw with the same crew.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked: anyone with a link can open it, so send each link only to its person. If a short link leaks, the organizer can kill that one person's link without a redraw. Each short link deletes itself after about 13 months.
The organizer also gets one group link, for a manage page. Its record holds the group name, the budget, each person's name and short code, and any keep-apart pairs the organizer set, but no match of its own. Even so, each short code opens that person's link, so the group link can reach every match in the group. Treat it like a key to the whole draw. It deletes itself after about 13 months too.
One exception: a person running a draw they are not part of can open a list of the pairings from the manage page, after a warning screen and a confirmation that they are not in the draw. That confirmation is trust, not a lock: the page takes their word for it, and the list is meant to stay closed to every player, including an organizer who is playing.
The organizer can also create one link for the whole group, under its own separate code. It opens a page listing the group's names: each person taps their own name, confirms it is them, and sees only their own match. Anyone holding the link can see the names and can open a match by picking a name, so it is for groups that trust each other. The page marks each name once it has been opened, and opening a name again asks for the same confirmation. That link cannot open the manage page or the pairings list, and its record holds no names or matches of its own, only a note of which names have been opened through it.
When a link opens, it leaves a note behind: a random code for that draw, plus the word opened or saw, and no name, no match, and no gift pick. The organizer's list reads those notes to see who still needs a nudge, and each note deletes itself after 120 days. You share links with your own apps, and sharing starts only when you tap a button.
Starting your own draw
After you see your match, the page offers a link to start your own draw. If you tap it, the names from the draw you were in are kept on this device for up to a week, so your new draw can open with those names already filled in. Nothing is kept for that unless you tap the link, and you can change or clear every filled-in name before you draw.
The Start your own draw link also carries your own private link's code, so another browser or another device can fill in the same names. Anyone with that link can open your match and see the group's names, so treat that link like your private link.
How visits are counted
This site loads Cloudflare Web Analytics, which sends page and performance counts to Cloudflare; Cloudflare says its beacon uses no cookies. The site also loads PostHog, which counts page views, draws, shares, link opens, card saves, pairings-list views, and group page views and name picks. It also counts return visits and Start your own draw taps.
Gift idea matches are counted as a count of picks only. PostHog counts actions only, never what you type. On a first visit it also remembers which site or app sent the visit: only that name, never the full link that was tapped. No names, matches, gift picks, or link parts are sent, and PostHog sets no cookie on this site.
Your browser also keeps one yes-or-no mark on this device. It says this browser has drawn or peeked before; it holds no names, matches, gift picks, or links, and it is what lets a later visit count as a return visit.
Your saved draw stays on this device too. It holds your names and each person's link, and it marks which links you have shared from this device. On a new draw it also holds the random codes the open-notes use, each person's short-link code, and your group link's code. It is never sent to us or to PostHog, and the counts never include anything inside it.
The ChatGPT plugin
The Pick My Secret Santa plugin for ChatGPT is published and live. Here is how it works. In the chat, you set the group up in words; the chat does the talking, and the draw still runs here, on this site. The plugin never draws and never assigns anyone.
If you give the chat your group's names, they pass through our server once. They are held in memory only, to build your pre-filled link, and they are never stored. Our server counts plugin tool calls by day, as counts only. The names also stay in your chat history, and that history is kept under ChatGPT's rules, not ours.
Children
Adults run the draws on this site. Some of the gifts here are for children, but the site is not directed at children under 13.

Questions about privacy: [email protected].

Privacidad
La versión corta: El sorteo se hace en tu navegador, y los sorteos nuevos también crean enlaces cortos. Para un enlace corto, nuestro servidor guarda tu nombre y tu asignación bajo un código al azar, de una forma que podemos leer; la dirección en sí no guarda nada que se pueda leer, pero nosotros operamos este servidor, así que podemos leer lo que está guardado. Quien tenga un enlace puede abrir la asignación de ese enlace, y el enlace de grupo del organizador puede llegar al enlace de cada persona, así que puede llegar a cada asignación. Cloudflare Web Analytics cuenta las visitas aquí, y PostHog cuenta sorteos, compartidos y aperturas de enlaces, solo como conteos. Un sorteo anota cuáles de sus enlaces se abrieron, solo por código al azar. Aquí no hay cuentas.
Qué hace el sorteo
Escribes los nombres, un presupuesto y las parejas que no deben regalarse entre sí, y las cuentas del sorteo se hacen en tu navegador. Para crear los enlaces cortos, nuestro servidor guarda cada nombre y asignación de una forma que podemos leer.
También puedes decir qué le gusta a una persona, con tus propias palabras. En la herramienta del sorteo, esas palabras se comparan en este dispositivo; no se envían ni se guardan, y ahí no se pide ningún nombre. Si usas el panel Ask en cambio, tus palabras van a la IA de este sitio, que las lee y elige de la lista de regalos del sitio, y nada de lo que escribas en el panel Ask se guarda.
Después de un sorteo, tu navegador guarda tus enlaces solo en este dispositivo, para que puedas enviar un enlace otra vez más tarde. Puedes borrarlos cuando quieras con dos toques. En un dispositivo compartido, bórralos cuando termines.
Enlaces privados
Cada enlace muestra la asignación de una sola persona, y la de nadie más. Con un enlace largo, la asignación va dentro del propio enlace, en palabras codificadas después del símbolo #. Esa parte no se envía a nuestro servidor cuando el enlace se abre, pero quien tenga el enlace puede leerla.
Los sorteos nuevos también crean un enlace corto para cada persona. La dirección de un enlace corto guarda solo un código al azar, y nada en ella se puede leer. Tu nombre y el nombre que te tocó quedan en nuestro servidor bajo ese código, de una forma que podemos leer; nosotros operamos este servidor, así que podemos leer los nombres y las asignaciones guardados para los enlaces cortos. Ese registro también guarda los nombres del grupo, para que quien abra el enlace pueda hacer su propio sorteo con el mismo grupo.
Un enlace está escondido de la vista, no bajo llave: quien tenga un enlace puede abrirlo, así que envía cada enlace solo a su persona. Si un enlace corto se filtra, el organizador puede desactivar el enlace de esa persona sin rehacer el sorteo. Cada enlace corto se borra solo después de unos 13 meses.
El organizador también recibe un enlace de grupo, para una página de gestión. Su registro guarda el nombre del grupo, el presupuesto, el nombre y el código corto de cada persona, y las parejas que el organizador marcó para que queden separadas, pero ninguna asignación propia. Aun así, cada código corto abre el enlace de esa persona, así que el enlace de grupo puede llegar a cada asignación del grupo. Trátalo como una llave de todo el sorteo. También se borra solo después de unos 13 meses.
Hay una excepción: una persona que organiza un sorteo en el que no participa puede abrir una lista de las asignaciones desde la página de gestión, después de una pantalla de aviso y de confirmar que no forma parte del sorteo. Esa confirmación es confianza, no un candado: la página se fía de su palabra, y la lista está pensada para quedarse cerrada a cada jugador, incluido un organizador que también juega.
Quien organiza también puede crear un enlace único para todo el grupo, con su propio código separado. Abre una página con los nombres del grupo: cada persona toca su propio nombre, confirma que es ella y ve solo su asignación. Quien tenga el enlace puede ver los nombres y abrir una asignación eligiendo un nombre, así que es para grupos que se tienen confianza. La página marca cada nombre cuando ya se abrió, y abrir un nombre otra vez pide la misma confirmación. Ese enlace no puede abrir la página de gestión ni la lista de asignaciones, y su registro no guarda nombres ni asignaciones propios, solo una nota de qué nombres se abrieron desde él.
Cuando un enlace se abre, deja una nota: un código al azar de ese sorteo, más la palabra abierto o visto, y ningún nombre, ninguna asignación y ninguna elección de regalo. La lista del organizador lee esas notas para ver quién necesita todavía un recordatorio, y cada nota se borra sola después de 120 días. Compartes los enlaces con tus propias aplicaciones, y el compartir empieza solo cuando tocas un botón.
Haz tu propio sorteo
Después de ver tu asignación, la página te ofrece un enlace para hacer tu propio sorteo. Si lo tocas, los nombres del sorteo en el que estabas se guardan en este dispositivo por hasta una semana, para que tu nuevo sorteo abra con esos nombres ya escritos. Nada se guarda para eso si no tocas el enlace, y puedes cambiar o borrar cada nombre antes de sortear.
Ese enlace también lleva el código de tu propio enlace privado, así otro navegador u otro dispositivo puede escribir los mismos nombres. Quien tenga ese enlace puede abrir tu asignación y ver los nombres del grupo, así que trata ese enlace como tu enlace privado.
Cómo se cuentan las visitas
Este sitio carga Cloudflare Web Analytics, que envía conteos de páginas y de rendimiento a Cloudflare; Cloudflare dice que su baliza no usa cookies. El sitio también carga PostHog, que cuenta visitas a páginas, sorteos, compartidos, aperturas de enlaces, tarjetas guardadas, vistas de la lista de asignaciones y visitas a la página del grupo y elecciones de nombre. También cuenta las visitas que vuelven y los toques en Haz tu propio sorteo.
Las coincidencias de ideas de regalo se cuentan solo como un conteo de elecciones. PostHog cuenta solo acciones, nunca lo que escribes. En una primera visita también recuerda qué sitio o aplicación envió la visita: solo ese nombre, nunca el enlace completo que se tocó. No se envían nombres, asignaciones, elecciones de regalo ni partes de enlaces, y PostHog no pone ninguna cookie en este sitio.
Tu navegador también guarda una marca de sí o no en este dispositivo. Dice que este navegador ya sorteó o ya miró antes; no guarda nombres, asignaciones, elecciones de regalo ni enlaces, y es lo que permite que una visita posterior cuente como una visita que vuelve.
Tu sorteo guardado también se queda en este dispositivo. Guarda tus nombres y el enlace de cada persona, y marca qué enlaces has compartido desde este dispositivo. En un sorteo nuevo también guarda los códigos al azar que usan las notas de apertura, el código de enlace corto de cada persona y el código de tu enlace de grupo. Nunca se nos envía ni se envía a PostHog, y los conteos nunca incluyen nada de lo que lleva dentro.
El plugin de ChatGPT
El plugin de Pick My Secret Santa para ChatGPT está publicado y activo. Así es como funciona. En el chat, armas el grupo con palabras; el chat hace la conversación, y el sorteo sigue haciéndose aquí, en este sitio. El plugin nunca sortea ni asigna a nadie.
Si le das al chat los nombres de tu grupo, pasan por nuestro servidor una sola vez. Se quedan solo en memoria, para armar tu enlace ya rellenado, y nunca se guardan. Nuestro servidor cuenta las llamadas a las herramientas del plugin por día, solo como conteos. Los nombres también se quedan en tu historial de chat, y ese historial se guarda bajo las reglas de ChatGPT, no las nuestras.
Menores
Los sorteos de este sitio los hacen adultos. Algunos de los regalos de aquí son para niños, pero el sitio no está dirigido a menores de 13 años.

Más: Inicio · Términos
Privacidade
A versão curta: O sorteio é feito no seu navegador, e os sorteios novos também criam links curtos. Para um link curto, nosso servidor guarda o seu nome e a sua combinação sob um código aleatório, de um jeito que a gente consegue ler; o endereço em si não guarda nada que dê para ler, mas a gente opera este servidor, então a gente consegue ler o que está guardado. Quem tiver um link pode abrir a combinação daquele link, e o link de grupo do organizador pode chegar ao link de cada pessoa, então pode chegar a cada combinação. O Cloudflare Web Analytics conta as visitas aqui, e o PostHog conta sorteios, compartilhamentos e aberturas de links, só como contagens. Um sorteio anota quais dos seus links foram abertos, só pelo código aleatório. Não há contas aqui.
O que o sorteio faz
Você digita os nomes, um orçamento e os pares que não devem se tirar, e as contas do sorteio rodam no seu navegador. Para criar os links curtos, nosso servidor guarda cada nome e combinação de um jeito que a gente consegue ler.
Você também pode dizer do que uma pessoa gosta, com as suas próprias palavras. Na ferramenta do sorteio, essas palavras são comparadas neste aparelho; elas não são enviadas nem guardadas, e nenhum nome é pedido ali. Se você usar o painel Ask, suas palavras vão para a IA deste site, que as lê e escolhe da lista de presentes do site, e nada do que você digitar no painel Ask é guardado.
Depois de um sorteio, seu navegador guarda seus links só neste aparelho, para você poder enviar um link de novo depois. Você pode apagá-los quando quiser com dois toques. Em um aparelho compartilhado, apague quando terminar.
Links privados
Cada link mostra a combinação de uma só pessoa, e de mais ninguém. Com um link longo, a combinação fica dentro do próprio link, em palavras codificadas depois do símbolo #. Essa parte não é enviada ao nosso servidor quando o link abre, mas quem tiver o link consegue lê-la.
Os sorteios novos também criam um link curto para cada pessoa. O endereço de um link curto guarda só um código aleatório, e nada nele dá para ler. Seu nome e o nome que você tirou ficam no nosso servidor sob esse código, de um jeito que a gente consegue ler; a gente opera este servidor, então a gente consegue ler os nomes e as combinações guardados para os links curtos. Esse registro também guarda os nomes do grupo, para quem abrir o link poder fazer o próprio sorteio com o mesmo grupo.
Um link fica escondido da vista, não trancado: quem tiver um link pode abri-lo, então envie cada link só para a sua pessoa. Se um link curto vazar, o organizador pode desativar o link daquela pessoa sem refazer o sorteio. Cada link curto se apaga sozinho depois de cerca de 13 meses.
O organizador também recebe um link de grupo, para uma página de gerenciamento. O registro dele guarda o nome do grupo, o orçamento, o nome e o código curto de cada pessoa, e os pares que o organizador marcou para ficarem separados, mas nenhuma combinação própria. Mesmo assim, cada código curto abre o link daquela pessoa, então o link de grupo pode chegar a cada combinação do grupo. Trate-o como uma chave do sorteio inteiro. Ele também se apaga sozinho depois de cerca de 13 meses.
Há uma exceção: uma pessoa que organiza um sorteio do qual não participa pode abrir uma lista das combinações na página de gerenciamento, depois de uma tela de aviso e de confirmar que não faz parte do sorteio. Essa confirmação é confiança, não uma trava: a página aceita a palavra da pessoa, e a lista foi feita para ficar fechada para todos os jogadores, incluindo um organizador que também joga.
Quem organiza também pode criar um link único para o grupo inteiro, com seu próprio código separado. Ele abre uma página com os nomes do grupo: cada pessoa toca no próprio nome, confirma que é ela e vê só a sua combinação. Quem tiver o link pode ver os nomes e abrir uma combinação escolhendo um nome, então é para grupos que confiam uns nos outros. A página marca cada nome depois que ele é aberto, e abrir um nome de novo pede a mesma confirmação. Esse link não pode abrir a página de gerenciamento nem a lista de combinações, e o registro dele não guarda nomes nem combinações próprios, só uma nota de quais nomes foram abertos por ele.
Quando um link abre, ele deixa uma anotação: um código aleatório daquele sorteio, mais a palavra aberto ou visto, e nenhum nome, nenhuma combinação e nenhuma escolha de presente. A lista do organizador lê essas anotações para ver quem ainda precisa de um lembrete, e cada anotação se apaga sozinha depois de 120 dias. Você compartilha os links com os seus próprios aplicativos, e o compartilhamento só começa quando você toca em um botão.
Faça seu próprio sorteio
Depois de ver a sua combinação, a página oferece um link para você fazer seu próprio sorteio. Se você tocar nele, os nomes do sorteio em que você estava ficam guardados neste aparelho por até uma semana, para o seu novo sorteio abrir com esses nomes já preenchidos. Nada é guardado para isso se você não tocar no link, e você pode mudar ou apagar cada nome antes de sortear.
Esse link também carrega o código do seu próprio link privado, para outro navegador ou outro aparelho poder preencher os mesmos nomes. Quem tiver esse link pode abrir a sua combinação e ver os nomes do grupo, então trate esse link como o seu link privado.
Como as visitas são contadas
Este site carrega o Cloudflare Web Analytics, que envia contagens de páginas e de desempenho para a Cloudflare; a Cloudflare diz que o beacon dela não usa cookies. O site também carrega o PostHog, que conta visualizações de página, sorteios, compartilhamentos, aberturas de links, cartões salvos, visualizações da lista de combinações e visitas à página do grupo e escolhas de nome. Ele também conta as visitas que voltam e os toques em Faça seu próprio sorteio.
As combinações de ideias de presente são contadas só como uma contagem de escolhas. O PostHog conta só ações, nunca o que você digita. Em uma primeira visita, ele também lembra qual site ou aplicativo enviou a visita: só esse nome, nunca o link completo que foi tocado. Nenhum nome, combinação, escolha de presente ou parte de link é enviado, e o PostHog não coloca nenhum cookie neste site.
Seu navegador também guarda uma marca de sim ou não neste aparelho. Ela diz que este navegador já sorteou ou já espiou antes; ela não guarda nomes, combinações, escolhas de presente nem links, e é ela que permite que uma visita posterior conte como uma visita que volta.
Seu sorteio salvo também fica neste aparelho. Ele guarda seus nomes e o link de cada pessoa, e marca quais links você compartilhou deste aparelho. Em um sorteio novo, ele também guarda os códigos aleatórios que as anotações de abertura usam, o código de link curto de cada pessoa e o código do seu link de grupo. Ele nunca é enviado para a gente nem para o PostHog, e as contagens nunca incluem nada do que está dentro dele.
O plugin do ChatGPT
O plugin do Pick My Secret Santa para o ChatGPT está publicado e no ar. É assim que ele funciona. No chat, você monta o grupo com palavras; o chat faz a conversa, e o sorteio continua rodando aqui, neste site. O plugin nunca sorteia nem atribui ninguém.
Se você der ao chat os nomes do seu grupo, eles passam pelo nosso servidor uma única vez. Eles ficam só na memória, para montar o seu link já preenchido, e nunca são guardados. Nosso servidor conta as chamadas das ferramentas do plugin por dia, só como contagens. Os nomes também ficam no seu histórico de chat, e esse histórico é guardado sob as regras do ChatGPT, não as nossas.
Crianças
Adultos fazem os sorteios neste site. Alguns dos presentes aqui são para crianças, mas o site não é dirigido a menores de 13 anos.

Dúvidas sobre privacidade: [email protected].

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/terms

Terms - Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
EN|ES|PT
Terms
These terms cover this website and its ChatGPT plugin. The site is a free Secret Santa tool: you add names and a budget, and it draws matches and suggests gifts. There are no ads, no accounts or sign-ups, and the site sells nothing at all.
How the draw works
The draw is random, with two rules: nobody draws their own name, and pairs you mark never draw each other. Some rule sets cannot form a draw, and the site will say so when that happens.
The ChatGPT plugin
Our Pick My Secret Santa plugin for ChatGPT is published and live, and this part tells you how it works. The plugin sets a group up inside ChatGPT and hands back one pre-filled link to this site. It never draws or assigns anyone; the draw happens here, on this site.
Where gift ideas come from
Gift ideas come from a fixed list: Santa's 212, drawn from the shared 255-idea bank it shares with The Present Picker. Your budget is a hard filter, and a gift hint raises matching ideas. Budget bands are guides, not exact prices; stores set real prices, and prices change.
Buying your gift
This site links to no stores. It takes no payment from you and places no orders for you. You choose where and what to buy, so check each idea before you buy it.
Accounts and data
How names, matches, and visits are handled is set out on the Privacy page.
No guarantees
This site is provided as is, and we give no warranty of any kind. We cannot guarantee any gift outcome, and we are not liable for any loss.
Fair use
Use this site only for lawful purposes, and do not try to break it. We may change or stop this site.

Cómo funciona el sorteo
El sorteo es al azar, con dos reglas: nadie se saca a sí mismo, y las parejas que marques nunca se sacan entre sí. Algunas combinaciones de reglas no pueden formar un sorteo, y el sitio lo dirá cuando eso pase.

Tu presupuesto es un filtro estricto, y una pista de regalo sube las ideas que coinciden. Las bandas de presupuesto son guías, no precios exactos; las tiendas ponen los precios reales, y los precios cambian.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/how-does-secret-santa-work

How Does Secret Santa Work? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
How does Secret Santa work?
One gift each. One name each. Nobody in the draw can see who has whom. Matches stay hidden until the swap.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
1Agree a budget
2Draw a name
3Buy one gift
4Swap day
The short version
Secret Santa is a group gift swap with the names hidden.
Agree a budget. One number everyone can afford.
Draw one name each. Your name is the only one you see.
Buy one gift. For your person only, inside the budget.
Swap on the day. Wrapped, labeled with their name, never yours.
That is the whole game. The secret is the fun part.
The rules most groups use
At least three people. Two is just a trade.
No one draws their own name. If it happens, draw again.
Label the gift with their name only.
Stay secret until the swap. Guessing is half the party.
Run it with this site
The draw runs in your browser. Our server stores each name and match for the short links, in a form we can read.
Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
Add every name. Add what each person likes.
Mark pairs to keep apart. Only if some must not draw each other.
Tap Draw the names. Each person gets one private link.
Send each link to its person only. The link shows just their match.
Each person also gets six gift ideas that fit the budget.
How the online draw works
Ways groups change the rules
Keep some pairs apart. Couples and close family often sit the draw out for each other. Mark the pairs before you draw.
Add someone late. Draw the whole group again and every match stays secret. Or a volunteer gives up their match, and the site names the price out loud: the volunteer tells the organizer their match. Both ways, in full.
White elephant is a cousin, not the same game. There, gifts are swapped and stolen in the open. Secret Santa is one secret match, bought for one person.
Reveal games. End the swap with a guessing game. See all eight reveal games.
Common questions
How many people do we need?
At least three. Three is the smallest group that works.
Can the organizer peek at the matches?
The screen itself does not show them. It shows names and links only.
Each match is shown only through its own private link.
The organizer holds every link and could open one. A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. What keeps it secret is that the organizer does not peek. One exception: someone running a draw they are not part of can open the full list from the manage page, after a warning and a confirmation that they are not in the draw.
What budget is normal?
Any one number the whole group can afford.
Most groups land between $10 and $30. Say the number before the draw.
What if someone forgets their person?
Their link still works. Links stay saved on the organizer device too.
The organizer can send the same link again.
Ready when you are
Start your draw

How to Run a Secret Santa — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
How to run a Secret Santa
The organiser's short list. Set it up once, then let the draw do the hiding.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
1Set day and budget
2Add names
3Draw and send links
4Swap and guess
The run, step by step
Pick the gift exchange day. Agree one gift budget.
Collect every name, and what each person likes.
Add the names here. Mark pairs to keep apart.
Tap Draw the names. Send each private link to its person only.
Post the draw receipt in the group chat.
On gift exchange day, end with a guessing game.
Before the draw
Set a buy-by date. A week before the exchange works for most groups.
Say the budget early. One number, the whole group, no exceptions.
Ask what each person likes. The tool takes likes in your own words, on step 2.
Ask about pairs. Mark them on step 3.
While you send the links
Send the group message first. It carries the budget and the rules.
Then send each private link to its person only.
Your share screen counts the links as you send them.
It names who still needs theirs, on this device only.
Closed the tab? Your draw stays saved on this device.
Open the site again and send the missing link.
On gift exchange day
Each gift is labeled with one name: the person it is for.
Nobody signs their own name.
End with a reveal game, and let the group guess.
See the eight reveal games
Keep planning
Secret Santa wishlist: one short note per person, saved on your device, never in a link.
Secret Santa reveal games: all eight guessing games, in full, to pick before the day.
I forgot who my Secret Santa is: the organizer can send the same link again.
When to start Secret Santa: one budget, one gift day, and a buy-by date a week before.
Last minute Secret Santa: the whole draw in about 2 minutes.
Do you reveal who your Secret Santa was: pick the reveal game before the day.
How Secret Santa works: the game in four steps.
Secret Santa rules: the classic rules, plus the enforced ones.
Gift ideas under $50: real picks, by interest.
Secret Santa for large groups: one draw for up to 100 people.
Common questions
How long does it take to run a draw?
About two minutes to set up. Sending the links takes as long as your own messages take.
What if someone joins late?
Draw the whole group again, so every match stays secret. Or swap in a volunteer, who gives up their match and tells the organiser.
How do I prove the draw was fair?
Post the draw receipt to the group. It shows the group, the date, the names, and the budget. It shows no matches and no links.

Secret Santa Rules — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Secret Santa rules
The short list most groups play by, plus the rules the draw here enforces for you.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
3+people in the group
1budget for everyone
The classic rules
At least three people. Two is just a trade.
One budget. Agreed before the draw, the same for everyone.
One name each. Each person draws one name, never their own.
One gift. Bought for your person only, inside the budget.
Their name on the gift.
Secret until the swap. Guessing is half the party.
Rules this site enforces
No one draws their own name. The draw cannot deal it, ever.
Marked pairs stay apart. Pairs you mark never draw each other.
Impossible draws stop early. If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so. Nobody gets a link until the draw works.
One link per person. Each private link shows one match only.
Four budgets. Under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100, and over $100.
Agree these out loud
A buy-by date. The draw cannot set one for you.
What counts as the gift. Bought, made, or regifted? Say it first.
Late joiners. Decide now: draw again, or swap in a volunteer. Both ways, in full.
The reveal. Guess first, or open in turns? Pick one before the day.
What to watch out for
With three people, one match gives away the rest.
With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked.
Anyone with a link can open it. Send each link to its person only.
A new draw makes new links. Links from the old draw still work.
Keep planning
What if you draw your own name in Secret Santa?: here it cannot happen — the draw cannot deal it.
Can you swap Secret Santa names?: no swap button — the two honest ways, and their price.
Do you put your name on a Secret Santa gift?: their name only — yours stays secret until the swap.
How Secret Santa works: the game in four steps.
How to run a Secret Santa: the organiser's short list.
Gift ideas under $50: real picks, by interest.
Secret Santa for large groups: one draw for up to 100 people.
Common questions
What are the basic Secret Santa rules?
At least three people. One budget everyone can afford. Each person draws one name, never their own. Buy one gift inside the budget. Label it with their name only, and stay secret until the swap.
Can someone draw their own name here?
No. The draw here cannot give anyone their own name. If marked pairs make a draw impossible, the site says so before any link is made.
What happens when we draw again?
A new draw makes new links. Links from the old draw still work, and they show the old matches. Send only the new set.

Secret Santa for Large Groups — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Secret Santa for large groups
One draw holds up to 100 people. Each person gets one private link.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
What large means here
One draw here holds 3 to 100 people.
That covers most teams, classes, and clubs.
A bigger group splits into smaller draws.
Split by team, by class, or by table.
Each draw is its own game, with its own receipt.
Nobody crosses between draws.
Run the big draw
Collect every name, and what each person likes.
Agree one gift budget the whole group can afford.
Add the names here. Mark pairs to keep apart.
Tap Draw the names. Each person gets one private link.
Send each link to its person only.
Post the draw receipt in the group chat.
Your screen shows names and links. The full list of matches opens only for someone who confirms they are not in the draw.
Keeping it fair at size
No accounts to create. No emails to collect.
A count while you send. Your share screen counts each link as you send it, and names who still needs theirs.
A receipt for the whole group. It proves the draw ran. It shows no matches.
No single match list exists. Each match is shown only through its own private link. Your device saves the links, and a link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. What keeps it secret is that you do not peek.
Splitting a bigger group
Give each smaller group its own draw.
Use the same budget in every draw.
One organiser can run them all from one device.
Only the newest draw stays saved on the device.
Send one group's links before you draw the next.
Two ways groups plan
Gift ideas under $50: real picks, grouped by what they are into.
Common questions
How many people can join one draw?
One draw here holds 3 to 100 people. A bigger group splits into smaller draws, one for each team or table.
Do people need an account or an email?
No. Nobody needs an account, and nobody signs up. Each person only needs their private link, sent by the organiser.
Can the organiser see who drew whom?
Not on the screen. The organiser screen shows names and links, never matches. The draw receipt proves the draw ran, and it shows no matches. The organiser holds every link and could open one. A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. Matches stay hidden unless the organiser peeks. That is trust, not a lock.
What does it cost?
Nothing. The draw is free. There is no sign-up, and there are no ads.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/white-elephant-vs-secret-santa

White Elephant vs Secret Santa — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
White elephant vs Secret Santa
One game buys for a person. The other game fights over a pile.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
Secret Santa
One secret match. One gift for one named person.
White elephant
No names. Gifts sit in a pile, stolen in the open.
Side by side
Who gets the gift? Secret Santa: one named person. White elephant: whoever ends holding it.
How are names picked? Secret Santa: drawn in secret, one match each. White elephant: no names at all.
How do gifts move? Secret Santa: wrapped, labeled with their name only. White elephant: picked from a pile, then stolen in turns.
What stays secret? Secret Santa: who bought your gift, until the swap. White elephant: only what hides inside the wrap.
Where does it work? Secret Santa: any group, near or far. White elephant: one room, one pile, one crowd.
Pick your game
Pick Secret Santa when each gift should fit its person.
Pick Secret Santa when your group is spread out.
Pick white elephant when the stealing is the whole party.
Pick white elephant when gag gifts beat thoughtful ones.
The limits
This site runs Secret Santa only.
It draws one secret match per person.
It does not run a white elephant pile.
If your group picks white elephant, you need no draw at all.
Just set one budget, wrap the gifts, and gather in one room.
Keep planning
Secret Santa at work: one draw for the whole team.
How much to spend on Secret Santa: the four budgets, compared.
How Secret Santa works: the game in four steps.
How to run a Secret Santa: the organiser's short list.
Secret Santa rules: the classic rules, plus the enforced ones.
Yankee Swap rules: the steal swap under its other common name, step by step.
Secret Santa for large groups: one draw for up to 100 people.
Common questions
What is the main difference?
Secret Santa buys one gift for one named person, in secret. White elephant puts wrapped gifts in a pile, and players pick and steal in the open.
Which game does this site run?
This site runs Secret Santa only. It draws one secret match per person. It does not run a white elephant pile or stealing rounds.
Which game suits a remote group?
Secret Santa. Each person gets a private link, so the draw works when the group never shares a room. White elephant needs everyone in one place, watching the pile.
Can a group play both?
Yes, on different days. Run the secret draw for real gifts first. Save the pile game for the party itself.

Secret Santa Questionnaire — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Secret Santa questionnaire
Five short questions. Send them before you draw a single name.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
5questions to send
11interests to pick from
0answers collected on this site
The five questions
Copy these into your group chat or mail. Short answers are fine.
1. Are you in? Joining is a choice, so ask first.
2. What are you into? Pick one: cooking, tech, outdoors, games, fitness, travel, cozy things, books, science, music, gardening, or surprise me.
3. What budget suits you? Under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100, or over $100.
4. Who must you not draw? A partner, say. Pairs can stay apart.
5. Can you make the exchange day? Name the day in your message.
How to use the answers
Send the five questions above to your group.
Add each name as the answers come back.
Set one interest per person, from their answer.
Mark pairs who must not draw each other.
Draw the names.
Send each person their own private link.
Adding names in bulk? One person per line works.
Add an interest after a comma. Like this: Maria, cooking.
Interests are matched in your browser. Names and matches are stored on our server for the short links, in a form we can read.

Interest shapes the picks. Six ideas in the link fit it.

Pairs stay apart. Marked pairs never draw each other.

What this site does not do
This site has no questionnaire form.
It sends no questions and collects no answers.

Answers come back to you, never to this site.

The interest answer. Set it on that person's row, and their Santa's private link carries six gift ideas picked for it, inside the budget.

Pick the closest of the eleven interests, or pick surprise me. The draw knows cooking, tech, outdoors, games, fitness, travel, cozy things, books, science, music, and gardening.
When should I send the questionnaire?
Before the draw. Send it with your budget and gift exchange day, so nobody has to guess either one later.

Can You Add Someone to Secret Santa After the Draw — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Can you add someone to Secret Santa after the draw
Yes. Two honest ways, and what each one costs.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
Way one: draw again
Every secret kept. The cost is new links.
Way two: a volunteer swaps
One secret spent: the volunteer tells you their match.
The short answer
Yes, someone can join after the draw.
There are two honest ways, and only two.
There is no way to add just one link to a finished draw.
Way one: draw the whole group again
Add the new name to the group.
Draw the whole group again.
Every match is drawn fresh.
Send only the new set of links.
Old links still show the old draw.
Every match stays secret. This way costs no secret at all.
Tell the group only that the draw ran again.
Way two: swap in a volunteer
One person gives up their match.
The new person takes that match.
The volunteer buys for the new person instead.
The old match gets a new Santa.
Three matches change. The group hears nothing.
The price: the volunteer tells you their match.
You set the swap up by hand, so you learn those matches too.
One match is no longer secret.
Which way fits
Nobody has bought a gift yet? Way one. It costs nothing but new links.
Gifts are bought and links are out? Way two. Only three matches move.
Nobody will volunteer? Back to way one. Those are the two honest ways.
New to running one? Read how to run a Secret Santa.
Keep planning

Common questions
Can I just add one more link?
No. A finished draw has no way to add one link. Pick one of the two ways on this page instead.
If we draw again, do the old links stop working?
No. Links you already sent still work and show the old draw. Send only the new set, so nobody follows an old match.
Does the volunteer way break the secret?
Partly. The volunteer tells the organiser their match, and the organiser learns those matches too. The rest of the group hears nothing.
How many matches change in the volunteer swap?
Three matches change. The group hears nothing about which three.

How Many People Do You Need for Secret Santa — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
How many people do you need for Secret Santa
Three is the smallest group that works.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
3people is the smallest group that works. One draw here holds up to 100.
The answer first
At least three people.
Up to 100 in one draw here.
More than 100? Split the group into smaller draws.
The draw asks for at least three names. Fewer, and it will not run.
Why two does not work
Two is just a trade.
Each person would know exactly who has them.
There is no secret left to keep.
Buy each other a gift and call it what it is.
Three works, with one honest edge
Three people can draw, and nobody draws their own name.
Each person gets one private link with one match.
The edge, in plain words: with three people, one match gives away the rest.
Once you know your match, the other two fall into place.
Four or more keeps the secret stronger.
With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another.
That edge is printed on the Secret Santa rules page too.
Bigger groups
That range covers most teams, classes, and clubs.
A bigger group splits into smaller draws.
Split by team, by class, or by table.
Each draw is its own game, with its own receipt.
Nobody crosses between draws.
Running a big one? Read Secret Santa for large groups.
Small group tips that the draw supports
Shared first names? Add a last initial for shared names.
Pairs to keep apart? Mark them before the draw.
Too many pairs? The draw can block. If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so.
One budget for everyone. Under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100, or over $100.
Each person gets six gift ideas inside that budget.

Can the Organizer See Who Got Whom — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Can the organizer see who got whom
No: names and links only, never the matches. The one full list opens only for someone who confirms they are not in the draw.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
The organiser sees
Names, one private link per person, a count as links are sent, and — on new draws — which links have been opened. Never who anyone got: the matches are not listed on it.
The matches
Each one is shown only through its private link. The one full list sits behind a gate on the manage page, and it opens only for someone who confirms they are not in the draw. Your device saves the links, so what keeps it secret is that you do not peek.
The answer first
No. Your screen shows names and links only.
The full list of matches opens only for someone who confirms they are not in the draw. You can organize the draw and be in it yourself, and your match stays as secret as everyone else's.

Names. The people in the group.
Links. One private link per person, ready to send.
A count as you send. It counts your Copy and Share taps here.
A draw receipt. The group, the date, the names, the budget, and the pairs kept apart.
The receipt shows no matches and no links.
Your saved copy of the names and links stays on this device only, so you can send a link again later.
Why it stays off your screen
The draw is picked in your browser. To make the short links work, our server stores each name and match in a form we can read. That storage is not locked with a key.
Each link shows one match only, to the person who opens it.
The organizer opens their own link last, just like everyone else.

No. There are no accounts to make and no addresses to collect. Names and links stay saved on this device. The short links are also stored on our server, in a form we can read, so each link can open.
How do people get their match without email?
You copy each private link and send it in your own chat or mail. Each link shows one match only.
What if I close the tab before sending a link?
Your links stay saved on this device. Open this page again to send one. The short links are also stored on our server, in a form we can read, so each link can open.

Secret Snowflake Generator — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Secret Snowflake generator
The same secret draw. A winter name for it.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
1game, a winter name
0accounts to make
1private link per person
The answer first
Secret Snowflake is the same game. Everyone draws one person in secret and buys them one gift.
Groups pick the name for their setting. Offices and schools often use Secret Snowflake as the winter name for the draw.
Name your group Secret Snowflake. The draw, budget, and private links all work exactly the same.
The full draw is free. There is no sign-up at all. There are no ads.
Run the Secret Snowflake draw
Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
Add every name. Add what each person likes.
Mark pairs to keep apart, only if some must not draw each other.
Tap Draw the names.
Copy each private link from your screen.
Send each link in your own chat, to its person only.
Each person opens their link and sees one match, plus six gift ideas.
What the site never asks for
No account or password. There is nothing to sign up for.
No email addresses. Nobody in the group gives one.
Names are stored so links work. The draw runs in your browser. Our server then stores each name and its match for the short links, in a form we can read. That storage is not locked with a key.
Saved here too. Your browser saves your names and links on this device, so you can send a link again later.
You can clear them any time.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. Send each link only to its person.
What each person gets
One private link, sent by you.
Their one match, behind a cover screen first.
Six gift ideas inside the group budget.
Ideas come from a fixed list of 212 real ideas.
Budget bands: Under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100, and over $100.
Asking the group what they like first? Use the Secret Santa questionnaire.

Common questions
Is Secret Snowflake the same as Secret Santa?
Yes — the same draw under a winter name. Everyone is secretly assigned one person, buys one gift inside the budget, and the giver stays secret until the exchange.
Why do groups call it Secret Snowflake?
Some offices and schools prefer a name that is just about winter. The game does not change; only the name on the invite does.
Do I need to sign up or give an email?
No. There is no sign-up and no email, for you or anyone in the group. You send each private link yourself.
What if I close the tab before sending a link?
Your links stay saved on this device. Open this page again to send one. The short links are also stored on our server, in a form we can read, so each link can open.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/secret-santa-generator-with-exclusions

Secret Santa Generator With Exclusions — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Secret Santa generator with exclusions
Mark the pairs. The draw keeps them apart.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
Allpairs kept apart
0self-picks
1private link per person
The answer first
Yes, pairs stay apart. Mark pairs who must not draw each other.
Pick My Secret Santa is a free Secret Santa generator. It draws names in secret in your browser, and our server stores each name and match for the short links, in a form we can read — no sign-up, no email, no account for anyone. One draw holds 3 to 100 people, nobody draws their own name, and each person gets one private link with their match.
Copy these steps
Every pair is honored. A marked pair is never dealt by the draw.
Too many pairs can block the draw.
Run the draw with exclusions
Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
Add every name. Add what each person likes.
Mark each pair who must not draw each other.
Add another pair, or remove one, any time before the draw.
Tap Draw the names. The draw keeps marked pairs apart.
Send each private link to its person only.
Each person opens their link and sees one match, plus six gift ideas.
Who groups keep apart
Couples and partners. Two people who already buy for each other.
People who share a home. A surprise is hard to hide under one roof.
Last year's matches. Mark them apart, and nobody draws the same person twice.
One pair takes two names. Add as many pairs as the group needs.
The step is optional. Most groups can skip it and draw at once.
What to watch out for
Three people and one pair. With three people, one pair apart leaves no fair draw.
The site says so before any link is made. Its words: That draw cannot work.
Remove one pair you marked, and the draw runs.
Four people and pairs. With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another.
The receipt proves it. The draw receipt names how many pairs were kept apart.
It shows no matches and no links. Post it to the whole group.
The full rule list: Secret Santa rules.

Can I keep some pairs apart?
Yes. Mark pairs who must not draw each other; the draw keeps them apart. Too many pairs can block the draw.
Can couples or partners be kept apart?
Yes. Mark the two names as one pair before the draw. Neither of them can draw the other.
What if the pairs leave no fair draw?

Can You Resend a Secret Santa Link — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Can you resend a Secret Santa link
Yes. Your last draw stays saved on this device.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
1draw saved on this device
0accounts or emails needed
2taps to clear the saved draw
The answer first
Yes, from this device. Your last draw is saved on this device.
The short links are stored on our server, in a form we can read, so each link can open.
Send a link again any time, or share the receipt.
Close this tab, come back, and send a link again.
How resending works
Open this site on the device that ran the draw.
Find Your saved draw at the top of the page.
The saved list shows one card per person.
Each card names only its owner, outside its link.
Send that person's link again, to its person only.
The link still shows their true match.
Not sure who still needs one? The share screen names who still needs theirs.
The honest limits
Only the newest draw is saved.
Same device, same browser. The list lives in this browser, on this device.
A different device has no saved draw to send from.
Anyone on this device can open the links.
On a shared device, clear the draw when done.
Clearing takes two taps. Clear the saved draw any time.
Sent links keep working. Links you already sent still work, even after you clear.
Why the saved list lives here: Can the organizer see who got whom.
Lost your link?
Ask your organizer for a fresh one.
Only trust a link your organizer sent you.
Your organizer sees names and links only. The matches stay hidden from everyone in the draw.
Sending your link again shows them nothing new.

Common questions
Can you resend a Secret Santa link?
Yes. Your last draw is saved on this device. Send a link again, or share the receipt. The short links are also stored on our server, in a form we can read, so each link can open.
What if I close the tab?
Your links stay saved on this device. Open this page again to send one. The short links are also stored on our server, in a form we can read, so each link can open. Clear your saved draw any time.
Someone lost their link. What now?
Ask the organizer. Only trust a link your organizer sent you. The organizer can send the same link again from the saved draw.
Can I resend from a different phone or computer?
No. The saved draw lives on the device that ran the draw, so there is no saved copy here to fetch. The short links are stored on our server, in a form we can read, so each link can still open.
What if the saved draw was cleared?
Links you already sent still work. To send one again, run the draw again. A new draw makes new links. Send only the new set.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/secret-santa-generator

Free Secret Santa Generator — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Secret Santa generator
Type the names, and each person gets a private link showing only their own match. You can be in the draw too: nobody in it sees the matches, not even you. About 2 minutes, free.
Start your draw
Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.
0accounts to make
0self-picks
1private link per person
The answer first
Pick My Secret Santa is a free Secret Santa generator. It draws names in secret in your browser, and our server stores each name and match for the short links, in a form we can read — no sign-up, no email, no account for anyone. One draw holds 3 to 100 people, nobody draws their own name, and each person gets one private link with their match.
Say six coworkers join in. You add six names. You pick a $25 budget. The draw pairs each person once. Each person gets one private link. The link shows one match only.
You send the links. You send each private link yourself, in your own chat.
The full draw is free. There is nothing to install. There are no ads.
Run your draw
Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
Add every name. Add what each person likes.
Mark pairs to keep apart, only if some must not draw each other.
Tap Draw the names.
Copy each private link from your screen.
Send each link in your own chat, to its person only.
Each person opens their link and sees one match, plus six gift ideas.
What the site never asks for
No account or password. There is nothing to sign up for.
No email addresses. Nobody in the group gives one.
Names are stored so links work. The draw runs in your browser. Our server then stores each name and its match for the short links, in a form we can read. That storage is not locked with a key.
Saved here too. Your browser saves your names and links on this device, so you can send a link again later.
You can clear them any time.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. Send each link only to its person.
What each person gets
One private link, sent by you.
Their one match, behind a cover screen first.
Six gift ideas inside the group budget.
Ideas come from a fixed list of 212 real ideas.
Budget bands: Under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100, and over $100.
Asking the group what they like first? Use the Secret Santa questionnaire.

Common questions
Is this Secret Santa generator free?
Yes. The full draw is free. There is no sign-up. There are no ads. You send each link yourself.
Do I need to sign up or give an email?
No. There is no sign-up and no email, for you or anyone in the group. You send each private link yourself.
Can someone draw their own name?
No. The draw never pairs a person with themselves, and pairs you mark apart never draw each other.
How many people can join one draw?
One draw holds 3 to 100 people. Bigger groups split by team. Each team runs its own draw.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/gift-exchange-name-draw

Gift Exchange Name Draw — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Gift exchange name draw
Say your family swaps gifts. Eight names go into the draw. The draw pairs each name once. You mark partners apart first. Each person gets one private link. Each link shows one match only.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
How the draw keeps it fair
Rule
How the draw keeps it
No self draws
Nobody ever draws their own name.
Pairs apart
Marked pairs never draw each other.
One link each
Each link shows one match only.
No full list
The matches are never all shown to anyone in the draw; the one full list opens only for someone who confirms they are not in the draw.
Add at least three names. One draw holds up to 100. Pick a budget before you draw. Then send each link yourself. The draw is picked in your browser. To make the private links work, the names and matches are stored on our server, in a form we can read.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Is a name draw the same game?
Yes. A gift exchange is Secret Santa. One name drawn in secret. One gift bought for that person.
What if no fair draw exists?
The draw says so first. No links get made. Loosen one marked pair. Then draw again right away.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/dirty-santa-rules

Dirty Santa Rules — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Dirty Santa rules
Dirty Santa is a swap with steals. Each guest brings one wrapped gift. The group sets one price cap first. You open gifts in turn. A turn can end with a steal.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The rules, step by step
Bring one wrapped gift near the budget.
Write one number per slip. All draw one slip.
Number one picks a wrapped gift. They open it for all to see.
The next guest makes a choice. Open a new gift, or steal an opened one.
If your gift gets stolen, pick once more. Open a fresh one, or steal one back.
Most groups cap steals on one gift. Three steals in a round is the norm.
Play ends when every gift stands open.
Number one takes the last move. They may swap for any opened gift.
House rules bend these steps. Set the steal cap first. That one call stops most fights.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Is Dirty Santa the same as White Elephant?
Nearly. The name shifts from place to place. The steal game stays the same.
How is Dirty Santa not Secret Santa?
Secret Santa gives each guest one name in secret. This game fights for gifts in the open. No names get drawn at all.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/can-you-do-secret-santa-with-an-odd-number-of-people

Can You Do Secret Santa with an Odd Number of People? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Can you do Secret Santa with an odd number of people?
Yes. Odd numbers work fine. The draw is a ring. Each person gives to one person and gets from one person. Odd or even never enters into it.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Why the ring always closes
Every name goes in once. Every name gets drawn once. No one draws their own name — the draw cannot deal it, ever. With 5, 7, or 9 people, the ring still closes. Nobody is left out, and nobody is left over.
The only real floor is three
Two people cannot play — each would know the other's match. Three works, with one honest edge: one match can give away the rest. After three, any number works, odd or even.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Does an odd number leave someone without a gift?
No. Each person draws exactly one name, and each name is drawn exactly once. The count of givers always equals the count of gifts.
Can pairs change the math?
You can mark pairs to keep apart, like partners. If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so before anyone gets a link.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/what-if-someone-drops-out-of-secret-santa

What If Someone Drops Out of Secret Santa? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
What if someone drops out of Secret Santa?
It is fixable — if gifts are not bought yet. The clean fixes are the same two as adding someone late: draw the whole group again, or swap in a volunteer.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Way one: draw the whole group again
Take the name out and run the draw again. Everyone gets a new link. A new draw makes new links — and links from the old draw still work, so send the new ones and say plainly that the old ones are dead.
Way two: a volunteer swaps
One person agrees to give to the person who lost their Santa. Nobody else's match changes. This works best in small groups, where a full redraw feels like a big deal.
Tell the organizer early
Both fixes get harder once gifts are bought. If you must drop out, say so the day you know. Your own link just goes unused — it reveals nothing about anyone else.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
We already drew. Now what?
Draw again, or swap in a volunteer. It is the same pair of fixes as adding someone after the draw.
What if their Santa already bought a gift?
Then it is the group's call. The gift can still be given at the swap. Most groups would rather get the gift than follow the rule.

Do You Reveal Who Your Secret Santa Was? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Do you reveal who your secret santa was?
Most groups do — at the swap, after the gifts open. The name stays secret until then. Guessing who gave what is half the party.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Pick one reveal game before the day
This site offers reveal games for the swap: Guess first, Three clues, and Balloon pop. Five more games show in your link at the swap. Pick one before the day, so the end of the party has a plan.
Or open in turns
The other classic: each person opens, then guesses out loud before the giver owns up. Either way, the reveal comes last — after every gift is open.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Do we have to reveal?
No. It is your group's call. Some groups never reveal. Most do, because the guessing is the fun part.
When do we reveal?
At the swap, after the gift opens. Secret until the swap is the rule the whole game rests on.

How to Do Secret Santa with Family — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
How to do Secret Santa with family
One draw for the whole family. Each person buys one gift, for one person, inside one budget the whole family agrees on. Names stay secret until the swap.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The family run, step by step
Pick the gift exchange day. Agree one gift budget — most groups land between $10 and $30, and one number for everyone keeps it fair. Collect every name, and what each person likes. Add the names here. Mark pairs to keep apart — partners, say, or the same household. Tap Draw the names. Send each private link to its person only. On the day, end with a guessing game.
Kids can play too
The draw's bank holds 60 kid picks, so a child in the draw still gets ideas that fit. Set a buy-by date — a week before the exchange works for most groups — so nobody is shopping on the day.
Family far away?
Distance does not end the game. Run the same draw online and swap by mail or on a call — see Virtual Secret Santa.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Can kids play with the grown-ups?
Yes. Kids go in the same draw. The bank's kid picks mean their link still deals six ideas inside the budget.
What budget is fair for a family?
Any one number the whole group can afford. Most groups land between $10 and $30. Say the number before the draw.

Start your draw
A real small draw, from this site's own sample
Four friends in. Four private links out. Each match is shown only through its own link. The matches reach each person only through their own link; the one full list opens only for someone who confirms they are not in the draw. Inside Maya's link — an example preview — she got Tom, with six gift ideas inside the budget. A link opens for whoever holds it, so each link goes privately to its person. The organizer's screen shows the names and the links, never who got whom.
The honest edge of three
Three people can draw, and nobody draws their own name. The edge, in plain words: with three people, one match gives away the rest. Once you know your match, the other two fall into place. With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another. Four or more keeps the secret stronger.
Small group tips the draw supports
Shared first names? Add a last initial. Pairs to keep apart? Mark them before the draw — if the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so. One budget for everyone, and pick the reveal game before the day.

At least three people. Up to 100 in one draw here. Two is just a trade — each person would know exactly who has them.
Can pairs change the math?
You can mark pairs to keep apart, like partners. If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so before anyone gets a link.

When to Start Secret Santa — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
When should you start Secret Santa?
Start when your group can agree two things: one budget and one gift day. The draw itself takes about 2 minutes, any day you run it. The buying needs the lead time — this site's rule is a buy-by date a week before gift day.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The order that works, from the site's own run list
Pick the gift exchange day. Agree one gift budget — most groups land between $10 and $30. Collect every name, and what each person likes. Run the draw and send each private link to its person only. Set the buy-by date a week before the exchange, so nobody is shopping on the day.
Gifts going by mail? Start earlier
Mail each gift in a plain box, early. Holiday mail runs slow. Agree the mail-by day before anyone buys — the day is the group's to set, and this site holds no date for you.
Christmas this year
Christmas Day is Friday, December 25, 2026. The countdown at the top of this page counts the days in your own time zone.
Put the two dates in your calendar
For a Christmas gift day, the buy-by rule lands on Friday, December 18, 2026 — a week before the day.
📅 Add to your calendar — buy-by Dec 18 + gift day Dec 25
One tap subscribes you to the whole season: both dates land in your own calendar and stay there. Free, no signup. Google Calendar: Other calendars → From URL, then paste the link.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
How late can we start?
The draw takes about 2 minutes, so the draw is never the slow part. Leave room to buy: a week before gift day is the buy-by rule this site gives its own sample draw.
When is Christmas in 2026?
Friday, December 25, 2026. The countdown on this page shows the days left where you are.

Pick My Secret Santa

Secret Santa for remote teams
One draw for the whole team, wherever they work. No accounts for anyone. No sign-up, no work email needed. Each person opens a private link, mails one gift, and the team opens them together on one video call.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The remote run, step by step
Agree one budget and one mail-by day. Add every name, from three to one hundred people. Mark pairs who must not draw each other. Draw the names. Send each person their own private link — a link opens anywhere, any town, any time zone. Mail each gift in a plain, sturdy box, early. Meet on a video call and open together.
Why it works spread out
The draw runs in your browser. Names and matches are stored on our server for the short links, in a form we can read. Gift ideas come with the match — each person gets six ideas inside the budget. Remote and in-room mix fine, so a hybrid team plays as one group.
Reveal on the call
Video reveal fits a call. Each Santa films a short clip first. Start in a hat or a mask. Take it off and say your name. Play the clips after the last gift is opened. Guess first works too.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.

One draw holds 3 to 100 people. A bigger team splits into smaller draws, one per group or floor.

Do You Put Your Name on a Secret Santa Gift? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Do you put your name on a Secret Santa gift?
No. Their name only. The classic rule: put their name on the gift, and nothing of yours. You stay secret until the swap — guessing who gave what is half the party.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
What goes on the gift
The rules this site prints are short: their name on the gift. Secret until the swap. At the swap, each person opens, then guesses out loud before the giver owns up — that is when your name comes out, in person, not on the tag.
Mailing it? Keep the box plain too
Mail it in a plain, sturdy box. Write no return name or address. A name on the box gives the game away before the party starts.
Pick the reveal before the day
Groups here pick one reveal game before the day: Guess first, Three clues, or Balloon pop. The reveal comes last — after every gift is open.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
What are the basic Secret Santa rules?
At least three people. One budget everyone can afford. Each person draws one name, never their own. Buy one gift inside the budget. Label it with their name only, and stay secret until the swap.
Do we have to reveal at the end?
No. It is your group's call. Some groups never reveal. Most do, because the guessing is the fun part.

What If You Draw Your Own Name in Secret Santa? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
What if you draw your own name in Secret Santa?
Here, it cannot happen. No one draws their own name. The draw cannot deal it, ever. That rule is built in, always — it is not a setting you have to turn on.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
In a paper draw: draw again
The classic rules this site prints are short: each person draws one name, never their own. If it happens with names in a hat, draw again. That is the whole fix, and every group plays it that way.
What this draw does instead
The draw is picked in your browser, and the names and matches are stored on our server for the private links, in a form we can read. It deals one private link per person. Each link shows one match only, and a match is never the person's own name. If marked pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so before any link is made — nobody gets a link until the draw works.
Pairs are the one edge to watch
With three people, one match gives away the rest. With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another. Four or more, with no tight pairs, keeps the secret stronger.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Can someone draw their own name here?
No. The draw here cannot give anyone their own name. If marked pairs make a draw impossible, the site says so before any link is made.
What happens when we draw again?
A new draw makes new links. Links from the old draw still work, and they show the old matches. Send only the new set.

Can Couples Do Secret Santa? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Can couples do Secret Santa?
Yes. Couples play like everyone else — and the draw can keep them apart. Mark the two names as one pair before the draw. Neither of them can draw the other. Every pair you mark is honored.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Why groups keep couples apart
Two people who already buy for each other get no surprise from drawing each other. People who share a home have the same problem — a surprise is hard to hide under one roof. The exclusions page lists both as the pairs groups keep apart most, along with last year's matches.
How to mark a pair
Name your group. Pick a gift budget. Add every name. Mark each pair who must not draw each other — one pair takes two names, and you can add as many pairs as the group needs. Tap Draw the names. Send each private link to its person only.
The honest edges
Too many pairs can block the draw. With three people, one pair apart leaves no fair draw — the site says so before any link is made, in its own words: that draw cannot work. Remove one pair you marked, and the draw runs. With four people and pairs marked, one match can give away another.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Can couples or partners be kept apart?
Yes. Mark the two names as one pair before the draw. Neither of them can draw the other.
What if the pairs leave no fair draw?
If the pairs leave no fair draw, the site says so before any link is made. Remove one pair you marked, and draw again.
