How to Give a Secret Santa Gift Anonymously — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
How to give a Secret Santa gift anonymously
Their name only — and hand it over where you are not seen. Label the gift with their name, and nothing of yours. For every way below: use plain wrap, and print the tag. Handwriting gives you away.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Four ways to hand it over at work
Desk drop: leave it on their desk before work starts, and slip away before they sit down. Front desk hold: leave it with the front desk or mail room, with only their name on the label. Mailbox surprise: drop it in their work mailbox slot — small, soft gifts fit this way best. Gift table drop: put it on the shared gift table early, and arrive before your person does.
Sending it by mail instead?
Mail it in a plain, sturdy box. Write no return name or address — a name on the box gives the game away before the party starts. Post it early. Holiday mail runs slow.
Stay secret until the swap
The classic rule: secret until the swap. At the swap, each person opens, then guesses out loud before the giver owns up. That is when your name comes out — in person, not on the tag.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Do you put your name on a Secret Santa gift?
No. Their name only. Put their name on the gift, and nothing of yours. You stay secret until the swap.
How do I mail a Secret Santa gift without giving myself away?
Use a plain, sturdy box and write no return name or address. Mail it early — holiday mail runs slow.

Can You Swap Secret Santa Names? — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Can you swap Secret Santa names?
Not one match by itself. A finished draw has no way to edit or swap just one name. There are two honest ways, and only two — the same two this site gives for adding someone late or fixing a drop-out.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Way one: draw the whole group again
Every secret kept. Draw the whole group again, and every match is drawn fresh. Send only the new set of links — old links still show the old draw. Tell the group only that the draw ran again. Nobody has bought a gift yet? This is the way. It costs nothing but new links.
Way two: a volunteer swaps
One person gives up their match, and takes the other match instead. Three matches change, and the group hears nothing. The price, named out loud: the volunteer tells the organizer their match, and the organizer learns those matches too. One match is no longer secret. Gifts are bought and links are out? This is the way.
Someone dropped out instead?
Same pair of fixes. Draw again with the name taken out, or a volunteer gives to the person who lost their Santa. Both fixes get harder once gifts are bought — say so the day you know.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Can I just swap one match?
No. A finished draw has no way to swap or edit one match. Pick one of the two ways on this page instead.
Does the volunteer way break the secret?
Partly. The volunteer tells the organiser their match, and the organiser learns those matches too. The rest of the group hears nothing.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/secret-santa-wishlist

Secret Santa Wishlist — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Secret Santa wishlist
One short note per person, saved by the organizer — and never put in any link. In Step 2 of the draw, each person's row carries a wishlist note for their Santa. Wishlist notes stay on this device and never go in the links.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
Add a note, one person at a time
On Step 2, open the row's optional part — its label is: Add likes or a wishlist note — optional. The note field itself is labeled: Wishlist note for their Santa (optional). Type one short line. The field caps the note at 200 characters, so keep it to the thing itself.
Adding a whole list at once?
Paste a list instead: one name on each line. Add an interest after a comma if you want — Maria, cooking. A wishlist note can follow it, as a third part of the same line. The draw's own example runs: Maria, cooking, the blue scarf, size M.
Where the note shows up
When a Santa opens their match, a note saved for their person shows under the heading Their wishlist. The words under it are the site's own: Your organizer saved this note on this device. It was never sent anywhere, and it is not in your link.
The one honest limit
A note shows only when the Santa opens their link on this device — the organizer's device, the one the draw was saved on. Send the link to the Santa's own phone and the link still works: it shows their match and their six gift ideas. The note is not in it, by design, so it cannot show there. Groups who need the note seen plan for that: the Santa opens the link on the organizer's device, or the organizer reads the note out another way.
What people write
The site's own example is the whole guide: the blue scarf, size M. The thing, plus the one detail that picks the right one — a size, a color, an exact title. One line is enough; the six gift ideas in the link do the rest.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Does the wishlist note go inside the private link?
No. Wishlist notes stay on this device and never go in the links. The note was never sent anywhere, and it is not in your link.
Why can't my Santa see my wishlist note?
A note shows only when the Santa opens their link on this device — the device the organizer saved the draw on. On any other device the link still shows the match and six gift ideas, but no note rides with it.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/secret-santa-reveal-games

Secret Santa Reveal Games — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Secret Santa reveal games
Pick one game for the whole group, before the day. These eight are the games this site deals at the swap — they show in your link when gifts open. The reveal comes last, after every gift is open.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
All eight games, in full
Guess first. Open one gift at a time, in turns. Each person guesses their Santa first. Only then does the Santa speak up.
Tag clue round. Write one clue on the gift tag. Read the tag aloud before opening. The group guesses from the clue alone.
Three clues game. Each Santa gives three clues, one by one. Clues start hard and get easier. The person guesses after each clue.
Note inside the wrap. Hide a signed note inside the wrapping paper. Your person finds it while they open. Keep the outside of the gift blank.
Stand and point. After the last gift, all Santas stand up. Each person points at their best guess. Santas sit down when guessed right.
Balloon pop. Put each Santa name inside a balloon. Each person pops one after opening their gift. The name inside names their Santa.
Video reveal. Film a short clip before the party. Start in a hat or a mask. Take it off and say your name. Play the clips after the last gift.
All at once. Tell everyone at once after the last gift. No guessing, no games, all names together. A Santa can stay secret if they want.
Far apart? Two of them fit a call
Video reveal fits a call (the clip game above). Guess first works too. Each person guesses before their Santa speaks.
Pick it before the day
Pick one before the day, so the end of the party has a plan. Secret until the swap is the rule the whole game rests on — the game you pick only decides how the secret ends, not when.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Do we have to reveal?
No. It is your group's call. Some groups never reveal. Most do, because the guessing is the fun part.
When do we reveal?
At the swap, after the gift opens. Secret until the swap is the rule the whole game rests on.

Lo que no hacemos

No vendemos regalos ni nos quedamos con ninguna comisión.
Es gratis para grupos de cualquier tamaño, sin límite de personas que pagar para desbloquear.
¿Cómo se llama en tu país?
El mismo juego tiene muchos nombres:

Amigo invisible, España, Argentina y Uruguay. → Haz el sorteo del amigo invisible
Intercambio de regalos, así se dice todos los días en México.
Angelito, República Dominicana.
Cuchumbo, en Honduras y El Salvador, así se llama también el recipiente de donde se sacan los papelitos.

Preguntas frecuentes
¿El organizador puede ver quién le tocó a quién?
No en su pantalla. La pantalla de quien organiza muestra los nombres y los enlaces, nunca las asignaciones a nadie del sorteo. ¿Es gratis? ¿Necesito una cuenta o un correo?
Es gratis, sin cuenta y sin correo. No te pedimos ningún correo electrónico, ni a ti ni a quienes participan.
¿Cuántas personas se necesitan?
Al menos tres. Con tres personas, una asignación revela las demás, y la página te lo avisa. El máximo es 100 personas por sorteo.
¿Qué tan secreto es?
Piensa en una nota en un sobre, no en una caja fuerte. La pantalla de quien organiza nunca muestra las asignaciones a nadie del sorteo. Y hay que decirlo claro: para que el enlace corto funcione, la asignación se guarda en nuestro servidor junto con los nombres, de una forma que podemos leer. Un código difícil de adivinar no es una llave, y guardar no es cifrar. Quien tenga el enlace puede abrirlo. Quien tenga el enlace de gestión puede llegar a todos los enlaces, y así a todas las asignaciones.
¿Perdí un enlace? ¿Puedo reenviarlo?
Sí. Los enlaces quedan guardados en el dispositivo de quien organiza, así que puede volver cuando quiera y copiar de nuevo el enlace de cualquier persona.
¿Puedo evitar que ciertas personas se regalen entre sí?
Sí. Marca las parejas que deben quedar separadas, por ejemplo, parejas o quienes se regalaron el año pasado, y el sorteo las respeta todas.

Amigo Secreto sin Correo: Sorteo Online Gratis, Sin Registro | Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Amigo secreto sin correo ni registro.
Pick My Secret Santa hace el sorteo del amigo secreto sin pedirte ningún correo, ni el tuyo, ni el de nadie de tu grupo.
Empezar el sorteo
Sin correo. Sin cuenta. Sin descargar nada. Gratis, en unos 2 minutos.
Por qué sin correo funciona mejor
La mayoría de los sitios de amigo secreto te piden el correo de cada participante para enviar las asignaciones. Eso significa escribir bien 10, 15 o 20 correos, esperar a que el mensaje no caiga en spam, y entregarle a un sitio las direcciones de todos tus amigos.
Aquí no hay nada de eso:
No escribes ningún correo. Escribes solo los nombres.
Nada cae en spam. Tú envías cada asignación como un enlace privado, por WhatsApp o por donde ya hablas con tu grupo.
Nadie crea una cuenta. Quien recibe el enlace lo toca y ve a quién le tocó. Nada más.
Ejemplo: un sorteo de muestra, sin ningún correo
Esto es un ejemplo, no un sorteo real.
Un salón de clases organiza su intercambio: Sofía, Mateo, Lucía, Emiliano y Renata, con un presupuesto de $20. La maestra escribe los cinco nombres, ningún correo, y toca Sortear.

Estás en un sorteo de amigo secreto, presupuesto $20. Toca tu enlace privado para ver a quién te tocó regalarle: (enlace) Sin registro. Tu organizador no ve tu asignación en su pantalla: se muestra solo por medio de este enlace. No reenvíes el enlace: quien lo tenga puede abrirlo.
Cada familia toca su enlace y ve solo su asignación. Nadie escribió un correo, nadie esperó un mensaje, nadie creó una cuenta.

Preguntas frecuentes
¿En serio no piden ningún correo?
En serio. Ni para organizar, ni para participar, ni para ver tu asignación. No hay formulario de correo en ninguna parte del sorteo.
¿Entonces cómo recibe cada persona su asignación?
Con un enlace privado que tú le envías, por WhatsApp, mensaje de texto o el chat que ya uses. Tocar el enlace es todo lo que tiene que hacer.
¿Es gratis aunque mi grupo sea grande?
Sí. Gratis para grupos de 3 a 100 personas, sin pagar por desbloquear más lugares.
¿Qué tan secreto es?
Piensa en una nota en un sobre, no en una caja fuerte. La pantalla de quien organiza nunca muestra las asignaciones a nadie del sorteo. Y hay que decirlo claro: para que el enlace corto funcione, la asignación se guarda en nuestro servidor junto con los nombres, de una forma que podemos leer. Un código difícil de adivinar no es una llave, y guardar no es cifrar. Quien tenga el enlace puede abrirlo. Quien tenga el enlace de gestión puede llegar a todos los enlaces, y así a todas las asignaciones. Envía cada enlace en privado y pídeles que no lo reenvíen.
¿El organizador puede ver quién le tocó a quién?
No en su pantalla. Muestra los nombres y los enlaces, nunca las asignaciones a nadie del sorteo.
¿Perdí un enlace? ¿Puedo reenviarlo?
Sí. Los enlaces quedan guardados en el dispositivo de quien organiza y se pueden copiar de nuevo en cualquier momento.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/amigo-secreto-online

Amigo Secreto Online: sorteie os nomes grátis, sem cadastro
Pick My Secret Santa
Amigo secreto online, sem complicação
Sorteie os nomes do seu amigo secreto ou amigo oculto em uns 2 minutos. Cada pessoa recebe um link privado e vê só quem ela tirou. Sem cadastro, sem e-mail, sem baixar aplicativo.
Sortear os nomes
Grátis, sem baixar nada. Leva uns 2 minutos.
Ver um sorteio de exemplo
Exemplo: um sorteio de exemplo
Isto é um exemplo, não um sorteio de verdade.
Quatro amigas e amigos entram para a troca do escritório: Mariana, Diego, Camila e André, com um valor entre $25 e $50.
Entram quatro nomes. Saem quatro links privados:
Mariana
Link privado enviado
Diego
Link privado enviado
Camila
Link privado enviado
André
Link privado enviado
Dentro do link da Mariana, só a Mariana vê isto:
Oi, Mariana. Você tirou: Diego
Uma das seis ideias de presente no link dela: Outdoors, Insulated steel water bottle, 32 oz. Keeps drinks cold for a full day on the trail.
A tela de quem organiza mostra os nomes e os links, nunca quem tirou quem.
Começar o sorteio →
Como funciona
Digite os nomes. Adicione todo mundo que vai participar. Se quiser, defina um valor e pares que não podem se tirar, como casais.
Faça o sorteio. O sorteio é justo e secreto. Você vê os nomes e os links, nunca quem cada um tirou.
Envie os links privados. Cada pessoa recebe o próprio link e descobre quem tirou com um toque. Guarde o seu link de organizador como uma senha: ele mostra todos os links.
O que não fazemos
O sorteio é escolhido no seu navegador. Para que os links privados funcionem, os nomes e as combinações são guardados no nosso servidor, de uma forma que conseguimos ler. Você envia cada link privado. Cada link mostra uma só combinação.
Nosso servidor guarda cada nome e cada par para os links curtos funcionarem, de um jeito que a gente consegue ler. Não vendemos dados e não pedimos e-mail de ninguém.
Não vendemos presentes nem ficamos com nenhuma comissão.
É grátis para grupos de qualquer tamanho, sem limite de pessoas para pagar e desbloquear.
Como se chama onde você mora?
O mesmo jogo tem vários nomes:
Amigo secreto, na maior parte do Brasil.
Amigo oculto, no Rio de Janeiro e em outras regiões. É o mesmo jogo, e esta página serve para os dois.
Amigo invisible, na Espanha, na Argentina e no Uruguai.
Intercambio de regalos, como se diz todo dia no México.
Seja como for que se chame na sua casa, o sorteio é o mesmo, e aqui é grátis.
Perguntas frequentes
Amigo secreto e amigo oculto são a mesma coisa?
Sim. O nome muda por região e por família, mas a brincadeira é a mesma: cada um tira um nome em segredo e presenteia essa pessoa. Esta página serve para os dois.
O organizador pode ver quem tirou quem?
Não na tela do organizador. Ela mostra nomes e links, nunca os pares. Cada link privado mostra só o par de uma pessoa, então compartilhe cada link só com a pessoa certa. Sendo honestos: um link fica escondido à vista de todos, não trancado a chave, quem tiver o link pode abrir, por isso cada link é enviado em privado, só para a pessoa dele. E é preciso dizer claramente: para os links curtos, nosso servidor guarda cada nome e o par dele de um jeito que a gente consegue ler. Guardar assim não é criptografar.
Precisa de cadastro?
Não. Ninguém cria conta e ninguém precisa de e-mail para participar.
Quantas pessoas são necessárias?
Pelo menos três. Com três pessoas, uma combinação revela as outras, e a página avisa você. O máximo é 100 pessoas por sorteio.
Quão secreto é?
Pense em um bilhete em um envelope, não em um cofre. A tela de quem organiza nunca mostra as combinações a ninguém do sorteio. E é preciso dizer claramente: para o link curto funcionar, a combinação é guardada no nosso servidor junto com os nomes, de um jeito que a gente consegue ler. Um código difícil de adivinhar não é uma chave, e guardar não é criptografar. Quem tiver o link pode abrir. Quem tiver o link de administração pode chegar a todos os links, e assim a todas as combinações.
Perdi um link? Posso reenviar?
Sim. Os links ficam guardados no aparelho de quem organiza, então ele pode voltar quando quiser e copiar de novo o link de qualquer pessoa.
Posso evitar que certas pessoas se presenteiem?
Sim. Marque os pares que devem ficar separados, por exemplo, casais ou quem se presenteou no ano passado, e o sorteio respeita todos.

## Page: https://pickmysecretsanta.com/yankee-swap-rules

Yankee Swap Rules — Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa
Pick My Secret Santa draws the names; each person sees only their own match.
Yankee swap rules
Yankee Swap is a swap with steals. Each guest brings one wrapped gift. The group sets one price cap first. You open gifts in turn. A turn can end with a steal.
Counting down to Christmas, Friday, December 25, 2026.
Start your draw
The rules, step by step
Bring one wrapped gift near the budget.
Write one number per slip. All draw one slip.
Number one picks a wrapped gift. They open it for all to see.
The next guest makes a choice. Open a new gift, or steal an opened one.
If your gift gets stolen, pick once more. Open a fresh one, or steal one back.
Most groups cap steals on one gift. Three steals in a round is the norm.
Play ends when every gift stands open.
Number one takes the last move. They may swap for any opened gift.
House rules bend these steps. Set the steal cap first. That one call stops most fights.
Some groups play a variant. Some let a player whose gift was stolen wait and pick again at the end. Some skip the first player's final swap. Name your group's variant before the first gift opens.
The honest part. The organizer holds every link. The organizer could open one. Links are hidden, not locked. It runs on trust, not a lock. Send each link to its person only.
Is Yankee Swap the same as Dirty Santa and White Elephant?
Nearly. Yankee Swap, Dirty Santa, and White Elephant are close cousins. The name shifts from place to place. The steal game stays the same.
How is Yankee Swap not Secret Santa?
Secret Santa gives each guest one name in secret. This game fights for gifts in the open. No names get drawn at all.

Pick My Secret Santa
Pollyanna gift exchange
Same game as Secret Santa. The Philadelphia-area name for it.

Free. No sign-up. About 2 minutes.

The answer first
Pollyanna is Secret Santa. Everyone draws one person in secret and buys them one gift.
The name is regional. Pollyanna is the Philadelphia-area name for a Secret Santa draw.
Name your group Pollyanna. The draw, budget, and private links all work exactly the same.
The full draw is free. There is no sign-up at all. There are no ads.
Run the Pollyanna draw
Name your group. Pick a gift budget.
Add every name. Add what each person likes.
Mark pairs to keep apart, only if some must not draw each other.
Tap Draw the names.
Copy each private link from your screen.
Send each link in your own chat, to its person only.
Each person opens their link and sees one match, plus six gift ideas.
What the site never asks for
No account or password. There is nothing to sign up for.
No email addresses. Nobody in the group gives one.
Names are stored so links work. The draw runs in your browser. Our server then stores each name and its match for the short links, in a form we can read. That storage is not locked with a key.
Saved here too. Your browser saves your names and links on this device, so you can send a link again later.
You can clear them any time.
A link is hidden from plain sight, not locked. Send each link only to its person.
What each person gets
One private link, sent by you.
Their one match, behind a cover screen first.
Six gift ideas inside the group budget.
Ideas come from a fixed list of 212 real ideas.
Budget bands: Under $25, $25 to $50, $50 to $100, and over $100.

Common questions
Is Pollyanna the same as Secret Santa?
Yes. Pollyanna is the Philadelphia-area name for a Secret Santa draw. Everyone is secretly assigned one person, buys one gift inside the budget, and the giver stays secret until the exchange.
Does this generator work for a Pollyanna?
Yes. The draw is identical. Name your group Pollyanna, add the names, and send each person their private link.
Do I need to sign up or give an email?
No. There is no sign-up and no email, for you or anyone in the group. You send each private link yourself.
What if I close the tab before sending a link?
Your links stay saved on this device. Open this page again to send one. The short links are also stored on our server, in a form we can read, so each link can open.
